title: Windows PowerShell output makes safe plugin paths look unsafe
original_report: On Windows, Hobbyka Hub 0.4.22 fails to install onec-direct-cli with: В архиве найден небезопасный путь.
expected: The safe onec-direct-cli archive installs on Windows.
actual: Windows PowerShell output decoded as UTF-8 contains NUL bytes and is rejected by the archive path guard.
environment: macOS arm64 reproducer simulating Windows PowerShell 5.1 UTF-16LE output; live windows-amd64 archive inspected
reproduction: The focused test passes a safe ZIP entry through the same UTF-16LE-to-UTF-8 mismatch and verifies that the production guard rejects it.
failure_signal: The regression test exits 1 because the Windows PowerShell command does not explicitly emit UTF-8.
root_cause: listArchive asks powershell.exe for entry names while Node capture always decodes stdout as UTF-8; Windows PowerShell 5.1 can emit UTF-16LE.
fix_summary: Set Console.OutputEncoding to UTF-8 before PowerShell writes archive entry names and bump Hobbyka Hub to 0.4.23.
why_causal: It makes the producer encoding match the existing Node decoder before path validation.

fix_files.summary: PowerShell archive listing now emits UTF-8.

checks.name: Focused regression
checks.detail: Exit 1 before the fix, exit 0 after it.

checks.name: Hub self-test and full plugin tests
checks.detail: Self-test and both Node tests pass.

checks.name: Live Windows archive integrity
checks.detail: onec-direct-cli windows-amd64 ZIP has safe paths and unzip reports no errors.

limitations: The focused test simulates Windows PowerShell 5.1 output because no Windows host is attached to this workspace.
residual_risks: A final install on Valera's Windows machine is still the strongest end-to-end confirmation.
notes: The onec-direct-cli package itself was not changed.
